module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_regfile
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Small synchronous MMIO decode and control/status register bank with byte-write masking, legal address decode, and fixed readback datapath. Use flip-flops only for the compact control plane and telemetry mirrors; no payload flattening or large storage.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Accept mmio_valid/mmio_write accesses, decode a compact 64-bit register window, update semantic config fields on legal writes, and return mmio_error on unsupported or malformed addresses. Preserve configuration until rewritten and present deterministic reset defaults for enable, launch, timeout, limits, fallback, sequencing, and IRQ policy.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain a minimal set of synchronous registers for enable, launch, reset/fault clear, sticky-fault policy, pipelined mode, outstanding limit, timeout/freshness thresholds, command bounds, fallback command, step limit, request type, sequence seed, operating-point metadata, session rollover, and status-clear control. Telemetry fields are read-only mirrors of downstream controller state.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive only semantic configuration outputs and MMIO response outputs. The module does not drive transport or actuator pins directly; its outputs feed the request packager, validator, timeout monitor, fallback controller, and telemetry block.
ownership_notes: Owns the MMIO-facing configuration and status plane.
Does not own request/response transport, actuator outputs, or interrupt generation directly.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_control_regfile.v

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_request_packager
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Small synchronous request constructor with one-hot-like issue control and a held-valid handshake. Compose a single 64-bit request word from sequence, request type, operating-point metadata, and compact identifiers.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Launch only when enabled and cfg_launch is asserted, while respecting outstanding-limit gating and optional pipelined mode. Once a request is issued, keep surrogate_req_valid asserted until surrogate_req_ready is sampled high; do not issue another request until policy allows it.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Retain the active sequence counter, request-hold state, and a minimal outstanding-issue indicator. Sequence numbering increments monotonically, with reset/seed behavior determined by the configured seed and session rollover policy.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive surrogate_req_valid and surrogate_req_data as RTL outputs, with req_launch_accepted and req_seq_active exported to downstream monitors. The request word is bounded and compact, never a bulk geometry payload.
ownership_notes: Owns outbound request packing and launch acceptance.
Does not own response acceptance, fallback, telemetry, or actuator outputs.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_request_packager.v

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_response_validator
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Synchronous response-checking datapath with simple extract/compare/clamp logic. Parse the 64-bit response into a sequence/token field and actuator suggestion field, then validate freshness and range before acceptance.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Accept only when surrogate_rsp_valid is high, sequence/token matches the active request, timeout has not expired, and stale-session/freshness conditions are clear. Reject malformed, stale, late, or out-of-range responses without updating the accepted command.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Track the last accepted sequence context, a small response counter, and acceptance/fault strobes. Use only compact arithmetic and comparators for sequence match, timeout relevance, and command bounding.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive surrogate_rsp_ready, rsp_accept, rsp_seq_match, fault classification bits, clamp activity, accepted bounded command suggestion, and response count. The accepted command remains a semantic suggestion and is not the final actuator output.
ownership_notes: Owns inbound response validation and bounded accepted-command suggestion.
Does not own the final actuator stage or fallback policy.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_response_validator.v

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_timeout_monitor
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Small counter-based age and outstanding monitor with synchronous increment/decrement behavior. Keep the logic intentionally simple: request-age counter(s), outstanding count, busy flag, timeout compare, and stale-session indication.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Start age tracking when a request is accepted, clear or decrement on response acceptance, and assert timeout_expired when the programmed threshold is exceeded. Detect stale-data conditions from request age, freshness threshold, and session rollover policy.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain the active request age, outstanding_count, busy status, timeout fault latch, and stale-session event. All counters reset deterministically and remain bounded to the configured small outstanding limit.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive request_age, outstanding_count, busy, timeout_expired, stale_session_event, and timeout_fault_latched for use by the validator, fallback controller, and telemetry.
ownership_notes: Owns timeout and freshness tracking plus the latched timeout fault indication.
Does not own MMIO configuration or transport handshakes.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_timeout_monitor.v

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_fallback_controller
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Deterministic safe-command selector with minimal fault retention logic. Use bounded compare/clamp/optional step-limit arithmetic only; avoid complex FSMs unless needed for sticky-fault retention and fault-clear handling.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Select safe fallback whenever disabled, in reset, on timeout/stale/protocol fault, or when the timeout latch is asserted. Allow fault_clear to release transient faults only when sticky-fault policy permits it. When a response is accepted, pass the validated bounded command forward if safe to do so.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Hold the current safe command, fallback_active, fault_active, and fault-classification bits. Preserve a stable fallback command across fault entry until explicitly cleared or superseded by a valid accepted command under policy.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive safe_cmd, fallback_active, fault_active, clamp_active, and fault_timeout/fault_stale/fault_protocol. The safe command is always bounded by the configured limits and never exceeds the controller envelope.
ownership_notes: Owns fallback selection and fault consolidation before actuator staging.
Does not own the actuator output pins directly.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_fallback_controller.v

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_actuator_output_stage
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Registered output pipeline with a stable final command register and a small mode encoder. Keep this stage purely sequential so the top-level actuator outputs are always driven by real RTL registers.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Capture the controller-selected safe_cmd and qualify actuator_valid/mode based on fallback_active, fault_active, and response-accept events. The stage never forwards an unclamped value and does not create combinational feedback into upstream logic.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain the registered actuator command, validity flag, mode encoding, and update pulse. On reset, initialize to the fallback default or conservative safe value and keep the output stable until a valid update occurs.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive actuator_cmd, actuator_valid, and actuator_mode as the final top-level actuator outputs. actuator_mode distinguishes normal closed-loop update, fallback hold, and fault-safe state.
ownership_notes: Owns the final registered actuator output path.
Does not own command selection or fault classification.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_actuator_output_stage.v

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_telemetry_status
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Lightweight telemetry aggregation and IRQ generation block with synchronous latch/level behavior. The design should stay simple: collect status fields, synthesize IRQ according to configuration, and expose stable readback values.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Assert status_irq on response acceptance, timeout, or fault entry according to register bits. Support synchronous clear through cfg_status_clear and reset, and do not alter control state while generating telemetry.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Mirror telemetry_state, busy, outstanding_count, last_seq, fault flags, clamp/fallback indicators, response count, and IRQ latch state. Maintain deterministic clear behavior and stable values for MMIO readout.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive status_irq only. Telemetry itself is supplied to the regfile as read-only inputs for status readback and does not feed back into control decisions.
ownership_notes: Owns IRQ generation and telemetry aggregation.
Does not own transport, control registers, or actuator outputs.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_telemetry_status.v

sequencing_notes: Request launch is a single synchronous issue event gated by enable and cfg_launch, then held valid until surrogate_req_ready is observed.
The request packager monotonically increments the sequence field and exports the active sequence for validation and timeout tracking.
The timeout monitor begins age tracking on request acceptance and clears/decrements on response acceptance; timeout and stale conditions are derived from compact counters and threshold compares.
The response validator only accepts valid, sequence-matched, fresh responses; accepted command suggestions may still be clamped and step-limited before use.
The fallback controller deterministically selects safe behavior on disable, reset, timeout, stale, protocol failure, or latched timeout fault.
The actuator output stage registers the final command and mode so the top-level actuator outputs always have real RTL drivers.
timing_notes: All logic is synchronous to clk with active-low rst_n and should be implemented using standard FPGA-flavored registers and comparators.

No combinational loop should exist between request and response handshakes; surrogate_req_valid and surrogate_rsp_ready must be generated independently of any direct combinational dependence on the opposing channel.
The request valid signal must remain asserted until ready is seen, which implies a held-valid register or equivalent synchronous hold behavior.
The output stage should register command, valid, and mode in the same clock domain to guarantee bounded and stable actuator outputs.
Any step limiting, if implemented, should be a small subtract/compare path with synchronous update only.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
